questions.question: On a centimetre grid, a parallelogram is drawn so that its bottom side (the base) stretches across 6 squares, and the straight-up distance from the base to the top side (the height) is 4 squares. Its slanted side measures 5 cm. Cut the triangle off the left end and slide it to the right end: the pieces now fill a rectangle that is 6 squares long and 4 squares tall. How many grid squares does the parallelogram cover?
questions.explain: Cutting and sliding turns the parallelogram into a 6 by 4 rectangle, so the area is base × height = 6 × 4 = 24 cm². The usual trap is multiplying by the slanted 5 cm side; the height is the straight-up distance, not the slant.

questions.question: A parallelogram sits on a centimetre grid. Its base runs along 7 whole squares, the straight-up height from the base to the opposite side is 3 squares, and the slanted side is 5 cm long. When the end triangle is cut off and slid across, the shape becomes a rectangle made of 3 rows with 7 squares in each row. What is the area of the parallelogram?
questions.explain: The rearranged rectangle has 3 rows of 7 squares, so the area is 7 × 3 = 21 cm². Many students grab the 5 cm slanted side instead of the 3 cm height — only the perpendicular height builds the rectangle.

questions.question: On a centimetre grid there is an empty rectangle 8 squares long and 5 squares tall, so it holds 40 equal squares in all. Beside it is a parallelogram with base 8 cm, height 5 cm, and slanted side 6 cm. The parallelogram is cut into one triangle and one trapezoid, and the two pieces are slid over to fill the rectangle exactly, with no gaps and no overlaps. How many of the 40 squares does the parallelogram cover?
questions.explain: Cutting and rearranging never changes how much space a shape takes up, so the parallelogram covers all 40 squares: 8 × 5 = 40 cm². The 6 cm slanted side is a tempting number, but the height 5 cm is what fits the rectangle.

questions.question: On a centimetre grid, Priya draws a parallelogram whose base covers 9 squares. The straight-up height from the base to the top side is 2 squares, and each slanted side is 3 cm long. She cuts the triangle off the right end and slides it to the left end to make a rectangle. Which sentence is true?
options: The rectangle is 9 squares long and 3 squares tall, so the area is 27 cm².
The rectangle is 9 squares long and 2 squares tall, so the area is 22 cm².
The rectangle covers fewer squares than the parallelogram, so its area is less than 18 cm².
The rectangle is 9 squares long and 2 squares tall, so the area is 18 cm².
questions.explain: Sliding the cut triangle makes a rectangle 9 squares by 2 squares, so the area is 9 × 2 = 18 cm². Watch out for the 3 cm slanted side — it is longer than the height and would give too big an answer.

questions.question: A parallelogram has a base of 12 cm, a perpendicular height of 7 cm, and slanted sides of 8 cm. Which calculation gives its area?
questions.explain: Cutting a parallelogram into a rectangle gives area = base × height = 12 × 7 = 84 cm². The 8 cm slanted side is not the height, and halving is for triangles, not parallelograms.

questions.question: Parallelogram A has base 15 cm, height 4 cm, and slanted side 5 cm. Parallelogram B has base 6 cm, height 10 cm, and slanted side 12 cm. Which statement about their areas is correct?
options: A is larger, because 15 × 5 = 75 cm² beats B at 60 cm².
They are equal — each has an area of 60 cm².
B is larger, because 6 × 12 = 72 cm² beats A at 60 cm².
A is larger, because its base of 15 cm is longer than B's base of 6 cm.
questions.explain: Each parallelogram becomes a rectangle of base × height: 15 × 4 = 60 cm² and 6 × 10 = 60 cm², so they match. Using a slanted side (5 cm or 12 cm) instead of the height inflates the answer every time.

questions.question: A parallelogram-shaped plot at a Surrey community garden has an area of 72 m². Its perpendicular height is 8 m and its slanted side is 10 m. What is the length of its base?
questions.explain: Since base × height = area, the base is 72 ÷ 8 = 9 m. Dividing by the 10 m slanted side is the common slip — only the perpendicular height pairs with the base in the rectangle.

questions.question: A parallelogram-shaped name tag has sides of 10 cm and 8 cm. The perpendicular height drawn to the 10 cm base measures 6 cm. Which calculation correctly gives the area of the name tag?
questions.explain: The height of 6 cm belongs to the 10 cm base, so cutting it into a rectangle gives 10 × 6 = 60 cm². Multiplying the two side lengths (10 × 8) measures nothing real, and (10 + 8) × 2 is the distance around, not the space inside.

questions.question: At a Kelowna school, students are painting a parallelogram-shaped panel on the gym wall. The panel's base is 5 m, its perpendicular height is 2 m, and its slanted side is 3 m. One can of paint covers 12 m². Is one can enough for a single coat?
options: Yes — the panel is 10 m², so one can covers it with 2 m² to spare.
No — the panel is 15 m² (5 × 3), so two cans are needed.
No — the distance around the panel is 16 m, which is more than 12.
Yes — the panel is only 5 m², because 5 × 2 has to be halved.
questions.explain: Cut the panel into a rectangle: 5 × 2 = 10 m², which fits inside the 12 m² one can covers. Using the 3 m slanted side would wrongly give 15 m², and halving is the triangle rule, not the parallelogram rule.

questions.question: Noah measures a parallelogram-shaped tile: base 14 cm, perpendicular height 6 cm, slanted side 7 cm. He writes 14 × 7 = 98 cm² for the area. Which response is correct?
options: He is right — multiplying any two side lengths gives the area, so 98 cm² is correct.
The 7 cm is the slanted side, not the perpendicular height, so the area is 14 × 6 = 84 cm².
He forgot to halve; the area is 14 × 7 ÷ 2 = 49 cm².
He should have added the base and height: 14 + 6 = 20 cm².
questions.explain: When a parallelogram is cut and rearranged into a rectangle, the rectangle's sides are the base and the perpendicular height, so 14 × 6 = 84 cm². The slanted 7 cm side leans, so it is always longer than the height and gives too large an area.

questions.question: Maya's rectangular sandbox measures 5 m by 7 m. Her neighbour's sandbox is a parallelogram with base 10 m, perpendicular height 3 m, and slanted side 4 m. Both are filled with sand to the same depth. Which sandbox needs more sand, and by how much area?
options: The parallelogram covers 5 m² more, since 10 × 4 = 40 m².
The rectangle covers 20 m² more, since the parallelogram is 10 × 3 ÷ 2 = 15 m².
questions.explain: The rectangle is 5 × 7 = 35 m² and the parallelogram cuts into a rectangle of 10 × 3 = 30 m², so Maya's is larger by 5 m². Using the 4 m slanted side would wrongly make the parallelogram the bigger one.

questions.question: A Victoria daycare is covering a parallelogram-shaped play patch with artificial turf. The patch has a base of 8 m, a perpendicular height of 2.5 m, and a slanted side of 3 m. Turf is sold only in full packs; each pack covers 5 m² and costs $12. What is the least the daycare can spend?
questions.explain: Area = base × height = 8 × 2.5 = 20 m², so 20 ÷ 5 = 4 packs at $12 each is $48. Using the 3 m slanted side gives 24 m² and pushes you to buy an extra pack you do not need.
